correctness.rationale: PASS: The a-point modulation Fourier transform separates residues u modulo a. The b translates within each residue give a circulant D_{q_u}, q_u=floor(r/a)+1_{u<r mod a}; squared singular values equal a|D_{q_u}(omega_b^j)|², with the zero and all-b cases handled by gcd(q_u,b)=1. For odd b, q=2 has extrema 2 and 2sin(pi/2b). The proof of the strict sampled Dirichlet inequality for each admissible q>=3 splits q even (j=(b-1)/2) and q odd (j near b(q-1)/(2q)), including q=3. Thus longer admissible boxcars have strictly larger B/A; exactly a+1<=r<=2a attain csc²(pi/2b), with A=4a sin²(pi/2b) and B=4a. For a=1 r=2 is included; b=3 boundary fine. This is a universal analytic argument, not an inference from finite singular values.
